rows.evidence: Q1: Sections III-VI, Tables 1-4 - the author compiles state-level data for 14 Indian states at four time points and runs his own correlation and OLS regressions of rural poverty on irrigated area per thousand rural population.
rows.notes: The study is about irrigation in general (gross irrigated area, irrigated area per thousand rural population) and its statistical association with rural poverty, real wages, foodgrain output and cropping intensity across Indian states. It contains nothing on drip or micro-irrigation, water consumption or electricity/energy use. No own result on the claimed effect.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections IV and VI, Tables 1, 3 and 4 - own regressions of state-level poverty and agricultural variables on irrigated area per thousand rural population for 14 states at four time points.
rows.notes: The study reports a positive regression relationship between general irrigation density (IAPTRP) and foodgrain productivity/output per head at state level (Table 1), but this concerns all irrigation, not drip or micro-irrigation, and is not a yield comparison of drip against another method. No evidence on drip and crop yield.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections IV and VI, Tables 1-4 - own cross-state regression analysis of irrigation and rural poverty.
rows.notes: The study contains no data or discussion on drip irrigation, weeds, pests or weed control. It analyses only state-level aggregate irrigation and poverty/wage/output variables.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections IV and VI, Tables 1-4 - own cross-state regression analysis of irrigation and rural poverty.
rows.notes: The study contains no data on drip irrigation, soil erosion or soil health. It is a statewise econometric analysis of general irrigation and rural poverty.

notes: The supplied text is Narayanamoorthy (2001), Indian Journal of Agricultural Economics 56(1), on irrigation (all types, measured as irrigated area per thousand rural population) and rural poverty across 14 Indian states. It does not deal with drip or micro-irrigation at all; the review probably intended a different Narayanamoorthy paper on drip irrigation economics. All four claim rows therefore fail Q2 with technology mismatch. Text appears complete (some duplicated paragraphs from OCR).
